messages.author: acb7c25298b3f6e1
messages.subject: Multiple person parameters?
parts:
Hi Phil,

I we want to create a custom item type using the createItem function, I was wondering if having multiple person parameters would technically always mean that we're dealing with a multidimensional model, although theoretically there is only one dimension of "ability".

For example, some IRT models take into account the speed at which the respondent has solved the item, those models usually have two person parameters: the usual ability parameter (theta) and the speed parameter (tau). If we want to model them together, does that mean that we are dealing with two "dimensions": speed and ability, or is it possible to understand this as simply two person parameters, both of which are unidimensional, but ability could theoretically be multidimensional? I understand that this may be a theoretical/philosopical question, but I'm not interested in such perspectives - I am simply interested in knowing how is it handled in mirt package.

I guess that my question can be rephrased as follows: does mirt allow for joint estimation of two probability trace functions within the same "item type"?

An example of what I'm trying to fit can be found here: https://www.jean-paulfox.com/Fox/documents/Papers/2010/APM%202010,%20327-347.pdf

Can the formulae (3) and (4) be fit under the same model?

messages.subject: Re: Multiple person parameters?
parts:
par <- c(1, 1) %>% 
  `names<-`(c("Beta", "Sigma"))

est <- rep(T, 2)

Theta <- matrix(seq(-6, 6, by=.2))

responses <- matrix(rnorm(nrow(Theta)*5, mean = 1.2, sd = 0.3), nrow(Theta), 5) %>% 
  data.frame()

time.fun <- function(par, Theta, ncat = 1){
  Beta <- par["Beta"]
  Sigma <- par["Sigma"]
  final <- map_df(responses, dnorm, mean = (Beta - Theta), sd = Sigma) %>% 
    as.matrix()
}

time <- createItem(name = "time", par=par, est=est, P = time.fun)

fit.times <- mirt(data.frame(responses), 1, itemtype = "time", customItems = list(time = time))
